events.did: loaded the last of the groceries into the pickup truck on his weekly supply run into town
events.quote_anchor: MITCH loaded the last of the groceries into the pickup truck.

events.did: drew the satchel from beneath the driver's seat and crossed to the diner on the corner
events.quote_anchor: He drew the satchel from beneath the driver’s seat and crossed to the diner on the corner.

events.did: answered the waitress who called him Jack by joking about whether the name would earn him many tips
events.quote_anchor: “Don’t know,” he’d said, “think it would earn me many tips?”

events.did: brought Jack a slice of peach pie and a glass of chocolate milk, teasing him about the drink
events.quote_anchor: She returned a few moments later with a slice of peach pie, and a glass of chocolate milk, teasing him lightly

events.did: drew the laptop from his bag, booted it up and connected to the diner's Wi-Fi
events.quote_anchor: Mitch drew the laptop from his bag, and booted up, connecting to the diner’s Wi-Fi.

events.did: opened a browser and typed in an address, bringing up the site The Fertile Plot
events.quote_anchor: He opened a browser, fingers moving briskly over the keys as he typed in the address, and the site came up.

events.did: skimmed the new gardening posts on the message board and then clicked over to his inbox
events.quote_anchor: Mitch skimmed the new posts—inquiries and debates about organic slug repellent, soil nitrate levels, the eventual midwinter thaw—before clicking over to his inbox.

events.did: wrote back a weather report to SHARPENEDSPADE1652 and waited a few minutes for the status dot to go from gray to green, but it stayed dark
events.quote_anchor: He waited a few minutes to see if the dot would go from gray to green.

relations.did: lives with Syd, who was suspicious when he picked the town of Herald
relations.quote_anchor: the smallest place he and Syd had ever stayed. She’d been suspicious when he picked it. And rightly so.

relations.did: and the waitress he calls Jenny both use names that are not their real names
relations.quote_anchor: amused by the fact that neither of their names was real.

relations.did: keeps biscuits for the stray dog Dol, which he caught with them
relations.quote_anchor: He caught a loose dog, thanks to the biscuits he kept for Dol

relations.did: sends status check pings to Mitch under the handle SHARPENEDSPADE1652, which Mitch answers from The Fertile Plot under the handle TURNINGOVERANEWLEAF
relations.quote_anchor: The usual status check. The text equivalent of a sonar ping.

numbers.did: had a population of 2,310 according to the most recent census
numbers.quote_anchor: According to the most recent census, the town—Herald—had a population of 2,310, which made it by far the smallest place

numbers.did: had spent two straight years in motels, short-term rentals and lock-and-leaves in big cities
numbers.quote_anchor: But after two straight years of motels, and short-term rentals, and lock-and-leaves in big cities, he’d wanted to try something new.

numbers.did: the weekly errands took him only an hour
numbers.quote_anchor: As usual, the errands had only taken him an hour.

numbers.did: donated twenty bucks to a local football team selling snacks to buy new uniforms
numbers.quote_anchor: donated twenty bucks to a local football team selling snacks to buy new uniforms.

numbers.did: told Jack her real name on his second visit to the diner
